comment: v2 socket ring. Retired with the freeform pegboard: the OBSERVE block and its 'no_observe' failure mode (observation is now automatic and SHOWN — every failing check's output visibly flows back into the agent's context mid-run) and the ESCALATE block. SQUINT AT IT inherits the subjective-verifier prose; the single STOP socket takes one config card instead of three stop blocks.

trigger.label: TRIGGER
trigger.desc: Starts the loop: schedule, file change, issue opened, CI failure, manual. Something has to ask.

agent.label: AGENT
agent.desc: The model edits the code. It is confident. Confidence is not a metric.

stop.label: STOP
stop.desc: How the loop ends. Seat a config card. A loop with no exit is called a career.

gate.label: HUMAN GATE
gate.desc: Pause for a person each iteration. Powerful once. On every lap, the person is the loop.

checks.label: RUN BUILD
checks.desc: The compiler reads every line and holds a grudge. Machine-checkable. It cannot be flattered.
checks.failLine: BUILD ✗ — 2 errors: 'ledger' is not defined. Neither is 'ledgar'.
checks.closerLine: BUILD ✗ — 1 error left. The grudge is narrowing.
checks.feedbackLine: the build errors flow back into the agent's context. It reads them. All of them.

checks.label: RUN LINT
checks.desc: Opinions — but codified, numbered, and enforced by a machine. That promotion makes them checks.
checks.passLine: LINT ✓ — 0 warnings. The style guide sleeps.
checks.failLine: LINT ✗ — 14 warnings, incl. one unused import carrying emotional weight.
checks.closerLine: LINT ✗ — 3 warnings left, all in the file it just touched.
checks.feedbackLine: the lint report flows back into the agent's context. It reads the warnings.

checks.label: RUN UI TESTS
checks.desc: A small browser opens and a robot clicks the button like a customer who has read nothing.
checks.passLine: UI TEST ✓ — the button does the thing. A robot confirmed it.
checks.failLine: UI TEST ✗ — clicked SAVE. Nothing saved. Screenshot attached, damning.
checks.closerLine: UI TEST ✗ — SAVE saves now. UNDO un-does slightly too much.
checks.feedbackLine: the failing screenshot flows back into the agent's context. It looks at it.

checks.label: SQUINT AT IT
checks.desc: A vibe with a socket. Accepts compliments. Returns opinions. Counts as nothing.
checks.passLine: SQUINT — looks good from here. (This proved nothing.)
checks.closerLine: SQUINT — still looks fine. Everything always has.
checks.feedbackLine: an opinion flows back into the agent's context. It was not information.

stops.label: ITERATION CAP
stops.desc: A maximum number of tries. Hope is not a maximum.

stops.label: SPEND BUDGET
stops.desc: A spending limit. The invoice arrives either way; this decides the font size.

stops.label: CAP + BUDGET
stops.desc: Tries capped AND spend capped. The loop ends on purpose, whichever limit arrives first.

stops.label: NONE
stops.desc: No cap, no budget, no exit but success. Optimism, socketed.

run.start: RING ENERGIZED. Current on the line.
run.triggerLine: TRIGGER — issue #4198: 'button does nothing (the main button)'.
agentLines: AGENT — reads the issue, edits src/button.ts. First attempt, full confidence.
AGENT — reads what the check said. Edits again, chastened.
AGENT — third pass. The checks steered; the agent merely drove.
run.stopLine: STOP — checks green. The loop exits on purpose. Under cap. Under budget.
run.squintPassLine: SQUINT — also looks good. Nobody asked, but it also looks good.
run.gateEscortLine: GATE — a human approved lap {n}. The human added nothing, warmly.

fork.title: THE LOOP FORK
intro: The road forks. One side is a LOOP. The other is a GRAPH. Two jobs are nailed to the signpost.
JOB A — FORMAT THE LEDGER. Known shape, known steps. A pipeline.
JOB B — THE WAGON WHEEL SQUEAKS SOMEWHERE. Nobody knows where. A surprise.

graph.hint: GRAPH side first. Seat PLAN, two parallel STEPs, and a MERGE GATE. Every node runs exactly once.

plan.label: PLAN
plan.desc: Splits the job into two halves. Once. Up front. With total certainty.

step_a.label: STEP
step_a.desc: Does its half. Exactly once. Asks nothing. Checks nothing.

step_b.label: STEP
step_b.desc: Does the other half. Also once. Also asks nothing.

merge.label: MERGE GATE
merge.desc: Waits for both halves, staples them together, declares the job done.

runA: GRAPH · JOB A — PLAN: split the ledger. Columns left, rows right.
STEP ‖ STEP — columns aligned; rows dated. In parallel. No drama.
MERGE GATE — both halves agree. Stapled.
DONE ✓ — ledger formatted. 6 tokens, one pass. The graph knew the shape of the job.
runB: GRAPH · JOB B — PLAN: 'a squeak is an axle problem.' Decided. Once.
STEP ‖ STEP — axle greased; bolts tightened. In parallel. With conviction.
MERGE GATE — both halves report success. Stapled.
The squeak continues. It was the door. Every node ran. No node listened.
graph.verdict: The graph is deterministic: every node runs once, the cost is predictable — and nothing in it can notice it was wrong.

loop.hint: Now the LOOP side. Seat real checks and a stop config, then RUN the same two jobs.
runA: LOOP · JOB A — lap 1: formats the columns. BUILD ✗ — a stray comma in the ledger parser.
lap 2: comma removed. BUILD ✓ LINT ✓ — rows still undated.
lap 3: rows dated. Checks green. STOP.
DONE ✓ — ledger formatted. 14 tokens. The loop paid 8 extra to double-check a job the graph already knew.
runB: LOOP · JOB B — lap 1: greases the axle. UI TEST ✗ — the squeak is audibly still there.
the failing check flows back into the agent's context. It stops believing the axle theory.
lap 2: follows the sound instead. It is the door hinge. Oils it. UI TEST ✓ — silence.
STOP — checks green. DONE ✓ — squeak found and fixed. Nobody told it where to look.
loop.verdict: The loop is adaptive: it costs more per job — and it is the only one that noticed.

tally: JOB A (pipeline) — GRAPH ✓ 6 tk · LOOP ✓ 14 tk. The graph wins on price.
JOB B (surprise) — GRAPH × shipped the wrong fix · LOOP ✓ converged. The loop wins on truth.
fork.banner: GRAPHS FOR PIPELINES. LOOPS FOR SURPRISES.
fork.moral: When you can draw the steps in advance, draw them. When you can't, build a loop and let the checks steer.

ridge.intro: The bridge is missing one plank. The gap is shaped exactly like a real check.
ridge.retreatDenied: There is no way back. The trail behind you has been deprecated.
ridge.squintDenied: SQUINT AT IT does not count. The bridge inspector is a machine. It cannot be flattered.
crossSuccess: The plank fits. Machine-checked. The bridge holds because holding is testable.
The party crosses while the loop runs on. Nobody watches. That was the point.
ridge.crossGated: You crossed. You personally inspected every plank. It took eleven days.
ridge.banked: +40 UNATTENDED MILES. THE PARTY SLEPT. THE LOOP DID NOT.

tutorial.prompt: You are a world-class principal staff senior engineer. Think step by step. Be correct. Do not be incorrect. My career depends on this. (revision 41, framed)
fires: PROMPT fired. 62% of the task appears, fully formed, in one pass.
It is genuinely impressive. The remaining 38% is load-bearing.
The same missing part is missing, with better formatting.
The prompt is now longer than the task.
tutorial.ceremony: Fort Prompt records this as its best result in two years. There is a ceremony.
tutorial.loopIntro: A settler whispers: some parties wire a CHECK to the output and feed what it says back in.
loopLines: LAP 1 — act. UI TEST ✗. The failure flows back in: 74%. It found the missing part by looking.
LAP 2 — act. UI TEST ✗, but nearer: 83%. No inspiration was involved.
LAP 3 — act. UI TEST ✗: 91%. The prompt has not changed once.
LAP 4 — act. UI TEST ✗, barely: 97%. The fort has gone quiet.
LAP 5 — act. UI TEST ✓: 100%. Done. Verified. Boring.
tutorial.banner: A PROMPT IS A WISH. A LOOP IS A PROCESS.
tutorial.moral: The loop did not need to be inspired. It needed to be told when it was wrong.

success.banner: THE LOOP RAN UNATTENDED. THE PARTY SLEPT.

no_verifier.banner: YOU HAVE DIED OF UNEARNED CONFIDENCE.
lines: STOP — success, reportedly. Nothing was asked to disagree.
Production reports the feature does not exist.
No check ever ran. The checkmarks were real, though.

subjective_verifier.banner: THE LOOP NEVER TERMINATED. IT LOOKED GOOD THE WHOLE TIME.
lines: SQUINT — does it look good? Define look. Define good.
SQUINT — good relative to what? The requirements also merely look good.
SQUINT — consider the ship of Theseus, if every plank were a refactor.
SQUINT — what is 'done'? A social construct with a deadline.
SQUINT — it looks the way the sea looks. Deep. Unknowable. Wet.
SQUINT — requesting additional tokens to continue looking.
subjective_verifier.drain: Tokens draining. The squint has opened a second line of inquiry.

no_stop_cap.banner: NOTHING TOLD IT TO STOP. NOTHING WILL.
no_stop_cap.iterLine: LAP {n} — fix applied. checks failing. trying again.
iterVariants: LAP {n} — a bold new approach: the previous approach.
LAP {n} — renamed a variable. hope levels: unchanged.
LAP {n} — the fix now has a fix. they disagree.
no_stop_cap.watch: The party watches the screen fill. The party says nothing.
lines: The loop is still running somewhere. It sends its regards.

breaker.banner: THE BUDGET BREAKER TRIPPED. THE CAP WOULD HAVE BEEN CHEAPER.
lines: STOP — the SPEND BUDGET slams shut at lap 10. 20 tokens, gone.
A cap would have called it at lap 3. The budget waited to be sure.

no_stop_budget.banner: THE WORK IS DONE. SO ARE YOU.
lines: LAP 1 — edit. checks: 2 failing. Retrying, expensively.
LAP 2 — checks green. Each check retried 40 times, to be sure.
STOP — under the cap. Something arrives with the sunrise.
no_stop_budget.after: The bill was always coming. The budget decides whether you meet it standing.

human_gate_everywhere.banner: IT WORKED. IT TOOK ELEVEN DAYS. YOU ARE THE BOTTLENECK.
lines: GATE — waiting for a human. (day 1)
GATE — approved: 'lgtm'. Next gate in forty minutes. (day 2)
GATE — waiting. Your calendar has opinions. (day 4)
GATE — approved from an airport. (day 6)
GATE — waiting. The human is at an offsite about velocity. (day 9)
CHECKS ✓ — pass. STOP. (day 11)
Every lap was safe. Every lap was you. You stood in the loop you built.

incomplete.missingStop: The STOP socket is empty: how does this end? Seat a config card. 'Eventually' is not a config.
